title: Vertical Farming
desc: Plan and run a small indoor or stacked farm: crops, light, water, nutrients, climate, food safety and business case.
outcomes: Explain how stacked growing works and what suits it.
Set light, water and nutrient schedules.
Compute yield, energy and water per kilogram.
task: Plan and run a small stacked growing pilot with schedules, logs, hygiene plan, harvest records and unit economics.
condition: A small space or shelving kit, lights, seeds, a spreadsheet, two peers and a grower mentor.
standard: Schedules are followed and logged; yield per tray recorded; hygiene plan applied; energy and water per kg calculated; cost per kg shown; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Growers, hospitality staff, school teachers, urban entrepreneurs.
evidence: plan, daily log, harvest record, cost sheet
modules: Not every crop suits stacked indoor growing.
Leafy greens, herbs and microgreens are fast, light and high-value.
Heavy crops such as grains and tubers are rarely economic indoors.
Microgreens are ready in about 8 days and sell at a high price per kg, suiting a small indoor unit.
Pick three crops and justify them.
Choose soil, hydroponic or aeroponic systems.
Hydroponics grows plants in nutrient water; aeroponics mists roots.
Parts: trays, pumps, channels, reservoirs, timers.
A timer controls a flood and drain tray that waters lettuce every 30 minutes.
Lettuce receives about 14 hours of light a day.
Keep water clean; change on schedule.
pH is kept between 5.8 and 6.2 using small adjustments.
Clean tools, hands and trays; keep pests out.
Mould appears at high humidity; fans and a dehumidifier fix it.
kWh per kg and litres per kg.
A tray gives 3.5 kg per cycle using 9 kWh per kg.
Setup cost, running cost, price per kg.
Price 250 INR per kg; cost 190 INR.
The pilot produces 62 kg of herbs.
quiz: Which crops suit?
Leafy greens, herbs, microgreens. (Covered in module 1: What suits vertical growing. To pass that module: Reasons given with numbers.)
Why LEDs?
Efficient, less heat. (Covered in module 2: Systems. To pass that module: Parts labelled.)
What pH range?
About 5.8 to 6.2 for many crops. (Covered in module 3: Light. To pass that module: Settings logged.)
Why hygiene?
Prevent disease. (Covered in module 4: Water and nutrients. To pass that module: Log complete.)
Yield measure?
Per m2 per cycle. (Covered in module 5: Climate and hygiene. To pass that module: Measures specific.)
Energy per kg unit?
kWh per kg. (Covered in module 6: Yield, energy and water. To pass that module: Maths correct.)
Biggest risk?
Pump or power failure. (Covered in module 7: Business case. To pass that module: Currency shown.)
Why compare to field?
See whether it pays. (Covered in module 8: Pilot plan. To pass that module: Peers follow.)
What is break-even?
Volume covering costs. (Covered in module 8: Pilot plan. To pass that module: Peers follow.)
Why log readings?
Spot trends. (Covered in module 8: Pilot plan. To pass that module: Peers follow.)
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: water management, alternative protein, greenhouse gas auditing.

ladder: What suits vertical growing

L1: learner can name crops. Focus module: What suits vertical growing (Understand, 3 h). Not every crop suits stacked indoor growing. Key points: Leafy greens, herbs and microgreens are fast, light and high-value. Heavy crops such as grains and tubers are rarely economic indoors. Weigh space, energy and market. Check local demand.

Teach: open with the worked example. Microgreens are ready in about 8 days and sell at a high price per kg, suiting a small indoor unit. Then set the activity: Pick three crops and justify them. Mark against the standard: Reasons given with numbers. Check at this level: Which crops suit? Model answer: Leafy greens, herbs, microgreens.
Systems

L2: learner knows system types. Focus module: Systems (Understand, 4 h). Choose soil, hydroponic or aeroponic systems. Key points: Hydroponics grows plants in nutrient water; aeroponics mists roots. Parts: trays, pumps, channels, reservoirs, timers. Failure risk if pumps stop. Cleaning between cycles.

Teach: open with the worked example. A timer controls a flood and drain tray that waters lettuce every 30 minutes. Then set the activity: Draw a layout. Mark against the standard: Parts labelled. Check at this level: Why LEDs? Model answer: Efficient, less heat.
Light

L3: learner can set schedules. Focus module: Light (Apply, 4 h). Plants need the right light. Key points: Intensity, spectrum and hours. LEDs use less heat. Distance matters. Photoperiod varies by crop.

Teach: open with the worked example. Lettuce receives about 14 hours of light a day. Then set the activity: Set a light schedule. Mark against the standard: Settings logged. Check at this level: What pH range? Model answer: About 5.8 to 6.2 for many crops.
Water and nutrients

L4: learner can run a tray. Focus module: Water and nutrients (Apply, 4 h). Balance matters. Key points: pH and nutrient strength checks. Keep water clean; change on schedule. Record readings. Adjust slowly.

Teach: open with the worked example. pH is kept between 5.8 and 6.2 using small adjustments. Then set the activity: Run daily checks. Mark against the standard: Log complete. Check at this level: Why hygiene? Model answer: Prevent disease.
Climate and hygiene

L5: learner can measure yield. Focus module: Climate and hygiene (Evaluate, 4 h). Prevent disease. Key points: Temperature, humidity and airflow. Clean tools, hands and trays; keep pests out. Separate harvest area. Dispose of waste.

Teach: open with the worked example. Mould appears at high humidity; fans and a dehumidifier fix it. Then set the activity: Write a hygiene plan. Mark against the standard: Measures specific. Check at this level: Yield measure? Model answer: Per m2 per cycle.
Business case
L6: learner can lead a farm shift. Focus module: Business case (Evaluate, 4 h). Does it pay? Key points: Setup cost, running cost, price per kg. Direct sales and contracts. Break-even volume. Risks.

Teach: open with the worked example. Price 250 INR per kg; cost 190 INR. Then set the activity: Build a cost sheet. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Energy per kg unit? Model answer: kWh per kg.
Pilot plan
L7: learner can audit a plan. Focus module: Pilot plan (Create, 3 h). Run 90 days. Key points: Targets and weekly reviews. Learn from losses. Decide to scale or stop. Share findings.

Teach: open with the worked example. The pilot produces 62 kg of herbs. Then set the activity: Present the plan. Mark against the standard: Peers follow. Check at this level: Biggest risk? Model answer: Pump or power failure.
